transcript.speaker: Donovan Reeves
transcript.content: Yeah — resourcefulness is the name of the game. A single strand of hair can work if you twist a few together and pull taut, but it’s fragile and not sterile, so use clean hair, be gentle to avoid damaging gums, and don’t reuse it. In a pinch I’ve used shoelace inner threads or fishing line while camping — stronger and cleaner — so it’s good to know multiple back‑ups rather than panic when your usual supplies aren’t available.

transcript.speaker: Benjamin Jackson
transcript.content: I get the ingenuity, but using hair as floss makes me uneasy — it’s fragile, not sterile, and could harbor bacteria or snap and damage gums. Shoelace inner threads or clean fishing line are smarter emergency substitutes if you have no floss, but they should be clean and used gently and once only. I’m all for resourcefulness, but I’ll still pack proper floss or interdental picks for trips — safer and less risky for your mouth.

transcript.speaker: Donovan Reeves
transcript.content: You’re right — I’m not saying hair is a replacement for regular floss, only that knowing safe fallbacks can save you from a bad situation. If you do need to improvise, use clean hair twisted tight or, better, a boiled/flame‑sterilized piece of fishing line or fresh shoelace inner thread, be ultra gentle, and don’t reuse it. I once had to clear a stubborn bit of food on a hike using a sanitized shoelace thread — painful afternoon avoided — so I stick with packing proper floss but keep a few of those backups in mind.

transcript.speaker: Benjamin Jackson
